questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'India's Parliamentary System' refers to.
questions.a: India follows a parliamentary form of government in which the executive is drawn from and answerable to the legislature; the Constituent Assembly debates of 1949 chose this model so that elected representatives directly control the government of the day.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'India's Parliamentary System'.
questions.a: The government sits in the legislature and answers to it - the heart of parliamentary democracy.

questions.q: Under which section is 'India's Parliamentary System' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 6 (source: hees106.txt lines 1-76 (constitutional choice, Constituent Assembly debates))

concepts.title: The Legislature: Parliament and Its Functions

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Legislature: Parliament and Its Functions' refers to.
questions.a: Parliament - the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha with the President - is the legislature that makes laws, controls finances, questions the government and represents the people; its legislative functions follow a bill's journey from introduction to presidential assent.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Legislature: Parliament and Its Functions'.
questions.a: Parliament debates, makes laws and holds the government to account on the people's behalf.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Legislature: Parliament and Its Functions' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: The Executive: President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Executive: President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers' refers to.
questions.a: The executive runs the government: the President is the constitutional head who acts on advice, while the Prime Minister and the council of ministers take real decisions; the Vice President presides over the Rajya Sabha, and ministers answer for their departments.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Executive: President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers'.
questions.a: Nominal head in the President, real power with the Prime Minister and ministers.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Executive: President, Prime Minister and Council of Ministers' taught, and from which source text?

concepts.title: Rights, Duties and the Working of Democracy

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Rights, Duties and the Working of Democracy' refers to.
questions.a: The parliamentary system works inside constitutional limits: the legislature and executive must uphold fundamental rights and follow the directive principles while making policy, keeping governance bound to justice, liberty and equality for all citizens.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Rights, Duties and the Working of Democracy'.
questions.a: Power flows within constitutional rails - rights and principles guide both parliament and government.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Rights, Duties and the Working of Democracy' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 6 (source: hees106.txt lines 290-347 (upholding fundamental rights and directive principles))
